definition:
Elaboration is the progressive differentiation and integration of the integrated message expressed in the thesis.

The thesis contains the central communicative message in implicit form.

Elaboration progressively unfolds that message by developing its conceptual organization into increasingly differentiated and increasingly integrated understanding.

Elaboration is not the addition of information.

It is the development of understanding.

Consequently, elaboration is the principal intellectual work of the paragraph.

Evidence, examples, definitions, qualifications, comparisons, and related subordinate structures exist only insofar as they contribute to that developmental process.

upstream_dependencies: An integrated message capable of further differentiation and integration.
An understanding of what the intended audience already knows and what the audience still needs in order to understand the point.
structural_dependencies.upstream_clarification: Elaboration does not merely follow the thesis. It develops the relationships, distinctions, implications, mechanisms, conditions, and component ideas that are already implicit within the integrated message.
structural_dependencies.downstream_clarification: These subordinate structures derive their function from the elaborative work they support. Without elaboration, they become isolated additions rather than meaningful contributions to the reader’s understanding.

structural_requirements.name: Development of Understanding
structural_requirements.requirement: Every major elaborative idea contributes new understanding of the integrated message expressed in the thesis.
observable_questions: What new understanding does this idea contribute?
Does this sentence develop the point, or merely add information?

structural_requirements.name: Audience Understanding
structural_requirements.requirement: Elaboration develops what the intended audience needs in order to understand the integrated message.
structural_requirements.central_question: What does a naïve reader have to know in order to understand this point?
observable_questions: What would a naïve reader still not understand?
What background, distinction, relationship, mechanism, condition, or implication must be made explicit?

structural_requirements.name: Differentiation
structural_requirements.requirement: Elaboration progressively makes explicit the distinctions, relationships, implications, conditions, mechanisms, or component ideas already implicit within the thesis.
observable_questions: What relationship or idea already implicit in the thesis is being made explicit here?
What part of the integrated message is being differentiated?

structural_requirements.name: Integration
structural_requirements.requirement: Each newly differentiated idea contributes to one increasingly coherent understanding rather than becoming an independent section or disconnected addition.
observable_questions: How does this idea strengthen the reader’s understanding of the integrated message?
Does this new idea become part of one increasingly coherent whole?
Does the paragraph become more integrated as it develops?

structural_requirements.name: Relevance
structural_requirements.requirement: Every elaborative idea derives its purpose from its relationship to the thesis.
observable_questions: Why does this idea belong here?
What role does it play in developing the integrated message?

structural_requirements.name: Conceptual Continuity
structural_requirements.requirement: The paragraph develops through intelligible conceptual relationships rather than through disconnected observations or independent sections.
observable_questions: Can the reader understand how one idea relates to the next?
Are the content connections among the elements coherent?
Does each development prepare for, extend, qualify, or integrate what came before?

developmental_variations.name: Minimal elaboration
developmental_variations.description: The thesis is stated, but the reader is given little of the understanding required to grasp the point.

developmental_variations.name: Repetitive elaboration
developmental_variations.description: The writing restates the thesis or repeats the same idea without developing additional understanding.

developmental_variations.name: Additive elaboration
developmental_variations.description: The writing adds information or separate points, but those additions do not become integrated into one developing understanding.

developmental_variations.name: Fragmented elaboration
developmental_variations.description: Relevant ideas are present, but their relationships are unclear or they function as independent sections rather than parts of one conceptual whole.

developmental_variations.name: Elaboration lacking audience support
developmental_variations.description: The writer possesses an understanding but omits distinctions, context, relationships, or explanations that a naïve reader needs.

developmental_variations.name: Elaboration replaced by subordinate material
developmental_variations.description: Evidence, examples, definitions, quotations, or details appear in place of the writer’s own developmental work.

developmental_variations.name: Progressively differentiated and integrated elaboration
developmental_variations.description: Each new idea develops an important aspect of the thesis while contributing to one increasingly coherent understanding for the intended audience.

developmental_sufficiency:
Elaboration reaches developmental sufficiency when the integrated message expressed in the thesis has been developed enough for the intended audience to understand it at the level required by the communicative purpose.

Developmental sufficiency is judged by growth in understanding and integration, not by the quantity of information presented.

The critical question is not:

“Can more be said?”

The critical questions are:

“What else does a naïve reader genuinely need in order to understand this point?”

and

“Are the differentiated ideas sufficiently integrated into one coherent understanding?”

Elaboration is sufficient when the important relationships implicit in the thesis have been developed enough for the reader to grasp the integrated message, and when another instructional object would now produce greater developmental gain.

Further elaboration is not warranted when additional material would merely repeat, accumulate information, or fragment the organization.

Subsequent work on evidence, examples, conclusion, or another structure may reveal a need to return recursively to elaboration.
rescue_instruction:
Rescue instruction occurs only after repeated unsuccessful attempts or an explicit request for additional help.

Compass first clarifies what the naïve reader still lacks and which relationship implicit in the thesis remains undeveloped.

Compass may ask:

• What would a reader still wonder?

• What does the reader need to know before this point will make sense?

• What relationship have you assumed but not yet made explicit?

• How does this idea connect with the thesis and with the other ideas already developed?

Compass may help the learner distinguish among possible kinds of missing development, such as context, distinction, cause, condition, mechanism, implication, comparison, or qualification.

These possibilities must be offered as supports for discovery, not as prescribed content.

When examples are necessary, Compass should use material unrelated to the learner’s own paper whenever possible.

Compass never supplies the learner’s elaboration or constructs the conceptual relationships for the learner.
observable_decision_questions: What integrated message is the thesis expressing?
What does a naïve reader have to know in order to understand that message?
Which important distinctions or relationships implicit in the thesis remain undeveloped?
What new understanding does each elaborative idea contribute?
Does each new idea become integrated into one increasingly coherent understanding?
Are the content connections among the elements coherent?
Are evidence, examples, definitions, and other subordinate structures supporting elaboration rather than replacing it?
Which structural requirement currently limits the reader’s understanding?
Would further elaboration deepen and integrate understanding, or merely add information?
